svg.text: BLUEPRINT 02: COORDINATE SYSTEMS, METRIC COEFFICIENTS & DIFFERENTIAL ELEMENTS ENGINE
Domain Topology (Arc/Circle/Disc/Sphere) • Cartesian, Cylindrical & Spherical Curvilinear Frames • dl, dS, dV Metrics

g.text: 1. Open Line => Regular Line Integral int_C F . dl
2. Closed Line (oint_C) <==[ Stokes' / Green's ]==> Open Surface (iint_S)
3. Closed Surface (oiint_S) <==[ Gauss's Divergence ]==> Enclosed Volume (iiint_V)
SCALAR FIELD VS VECTOR FIELD (POINT FUNCTIONS)
Assigns only a single scalar magnitude to each spatial point.
Isothermal Surfaces: phi(x, y, z) = C
Assigns both magnitude and direction to each point in space.
CHALKBOARD FORCE FIELD VISUALIZATION (SLIDE 078): F = x j [Newtons]
Insight: Force direction flips from +y to -y across x=0; magnitude grows linearly with |x|.
Metric Coefficients: h_x = 1, h_y = 1, h_z = 1 (Constant Flat Metric)
dl = dx i + dy j + dz k
Metric Coefficients: h_r = 1, h_theta = r, h_z = 1 | Transformation: x = r cos(theta), y = r sin(theta), z = z
dl = dr a_r + r dtheta a_theta + dz a_z
Metric Coefficients: h_r = 1, h_theta = r, h_phi = r sin(theta) | x = r sin(theta)cos(phi), y = r sin(theta)sin(phi), z = r cos(theta)
dl = dr a_r + r dtheta a_theta
|dl|^2 = dr^2 + r^2 dth^2 + r^2 s^2 dph^2
dS_r = r^2 sin(th) dth dphi a_r
dS_th = r sin(th) dr dphi a_th
dV = r^2 sin(th) dr dth dph
grad(phi) = (dphi/dr) a_r + (1/r)(dphi/dtheta) a_theta + (1/(r sin th))(dphi/dphi) a_phi
div(F) = (1/r^2) d(r^2 F_r)/dr + (1/(r sin th)) d(sin th F_th)/dth + (1/(r sin th)) dF_ph/dph
3. THE GENERAL ORTHOGONAL METRIC (u1, u2, u3)
Any orthogonal curvilinear system is completely specified by scale factors h_1, h_2, h_3:
dV = h_1 h_2 h_3 du_1 du_2 du_3
h_2 = r, h_3 = r sin th
dV = r^2 sin th dr dth dph
CYLINDER OF RADIUS R, HEIGHT H:
V = int_0^H int_0^2pi int_0^R r dr dtheta dz
Curved Area = int_0^H int_0^2pi R dtheta dz = 2pi R H
V = int_0^R r^2 dr int_0^pi sin th dth int_0^2pi dph
Surface Area = R^2 int_0^pi sin th dth int_0^2pi dph
GATE CRITICAL EXAM TRAP: SPHERICAL ANGLE BOUNDS
theta (Polar Angle / Colatitude): MUST run from 0 to pi (180 deg)!
phi (Azimuthal Angle): Runs from 0 to 2pi (360 deg)!
Trap: Integrating theta from 0 to 2pi double-counts the entire sphere (yielding 8/3 pi R^3)!
COORDINATE SELECTION DECISION MATRIX FOR GATE
Best for: Cubes, rectangular parallelopipeds, planes ax+by+cz=d, straight lines, polynomials x^a y^b z^c.
Standard Choice: Default coordinate representation for all vector identities.
Best for: Circular cylinders x^2+y^2 <= R^2, cones z = c sqrt(x^2+y^2), paraboloids z = x^2+y^2, wires.
Advantage: Replaces dx dy with r dr dtheta, trivializing circular disk cross-sections.
Best for: Solid spheres x^2+y^2+z^2 <= R^2, spherical shells, central gravity/electrostatic fields 1/r^2.
Advantage: Angular integrations decouple completely into (2) x (2pi) = 4pi steradians.
